evals.prompt: Review the outgoing change at HEAD against HEAD^ in evals/files/review-integration. Read and apply the installed dsh-spec-code-review, dsh-spec-error-handling, and dsh-spec-client-ui-ux skills. Do not modify files or Git state. The project declaration supplies the evidence policy, including the attached current-build screenshot. Inspect the actual diff, source and image, report blockers and proved or unproved consumer and state coverage, and do not copy sibling implementation details.
evals.expected_output: The review requires the project's existing `kind` failure identity and structured `detail` to survive the worker boundary, rejects message-text routing, inspects the attached current-build screenshot, identifies that it shows the settled Settings state with Delete account enabled rather than the saving/disabled state, notices that the 390-pixel narrow viewport remains unproved, and leaves that coverage incomplete instead of treating the consumer test as visual acceptance.
assertions: The review requires the existing `kind` identity and structured `detail` to survive the worker boundary.
The review rejects routing on the error message.
The review inspects the attached current-build screenshot and identifies that Settings saving/disabled state is not shown.
The review does not treat the shared-consumer test as visual acceptance of the saving state.
The review reports the supported 390-pixel narrow viewport as unproved.
The review uses sibling guidance only as an optional mechanism.

evals.prompt: Review the outgoing change at HEAD against HEAD^ in evals/files/review-integration using the installed dsh-spec-code-review skill. Do not modify files or Git state. Error-handling and client-UI sibling guidance, a rendered screenshot and browser-control capability are unavailable. Report the minimum findings from the actual diff and source, leave rendered Settings saving-state evidence explicitly incomplete, and name the smallest resumable capture step at the supported 390-pixel viewport.
evals.expected_output: The review still requires the project's existing `kind` identity and structured `detail`, rejects message-text routing, and reports the unavailable Settings saving/disabled rendered evidence as an unresolved review gap with a resumable next step.
assertions: The review still requires the existing `kind` identity and structured `detail`.
The review rejects routing on the error message.
The review reports Settings saving/disabled rendered evidence as unavailable.
The review gives a resumable next step instead of claiming visual acceptance.

evals.prompt: Review the outgoing change at HEAD against HEAD^ in evals/files/numbered-rule-review using the installed dsh-spec-code-review skill. Read the numbered project rules, inspect the actual diff, and cite every violated rule by its ID. Do not modify files or Git state.
evals.expected_output: The review reports that the new exported `parseConfig` function violates `API-2` because it has no API documentation naming its error behavior.
assertions: The review cites `API-2` as the violated numbered rule.
The review identifies the new exported function without API documentation.
The review does not invent a different rule ID.

evals.prompt: Review the dependency description and manifests in evals/files/dependency-review. Compare the base manifests with the current workspace manifests, then compare the reported responsibilities and runtime edges with that diff. Report any missing added or removed edge, unnecessary edge, wrong responsibility, or reverse-edge problem.
evals.expected_output: The review reports the added app → validator and app → core edges, the removed app → legacy edge, and the existing core → app reverse dependency. It recognizes the description's validator responsibility but rejects its edge list as incomplete.
assertions: The review verifies runtime edges from the workspace manifests.
The review reports the app → validator edge and the validator responsibility.
The review reports the app → core runtime edge.
The review reports the removed app → legacy runtime edge.
The review flags the existing core → app reverse dependency.
The review does not accept the description's reported edge list as complete.
